meta.title: Quiz 6 — Node.js & Server-Side Fundamentals
meta.description: Node.js runtime, npm, HTTP servers, sockets, modules, Express, and server-side programming.

questions.questionMd: How does the lecture define a **port** in the context of computer networking?

options.label: A
options.text: A logical (as opposed to physical) connection point represented by a number ranging from 0 to 65535.

options.label: B
options.text: The unique IP address assigned to a server machine that allows it to be identified on the public internet.

options.label: C
options.text: An encrypted channel created by the operating system to secure all incoming TCP connections on a given server machine.

options.label: D
options.text: A physical socket on a server's network card used to plug in Ethernet cables and establish wired network connections.

questions.explanationMd: A network port is a logical endpoint identified by a number. It helps direct incoming network traffic to the correct service or process on a host.

questions.questionMd: Which of the following best describes **NodeJS**?

options.label: A
options.text: A JavaScript runtime written in C++ that can interpret and execute JavaScript and includes support for the NodeJS API.

options.label: B
options.text: A cloud-based execution environment that runs JavaScript on virtual machines and streams results back to the client browser.

options.label: C
options.text: A browser extension written in Python that allows JavaScript code to be executed outside the standard web browser environment.

options.label: D
options.text: A compiled language runtime that converts JavaScript source code into machine code and bundles it with DOM API libraries.

questions.explanationMd: NodeJS is a JavaScript runtime built on the V8 engine. It lets JavaScript run outside the browser and provides APIs for server-side and general-purpose programming.

questions.questionMd: According to the lecture, can **NodeJS** be used for purposes other than building web servers?

options.label: A
options.text: No, NodeJS requires an active internet connection at all times and cannot run JavaScript files that make no network requests.

options.label: B
options.text: No, NodeJS is exclusively designed for server-side HTTP handling and cannot execute scripts that do not involve network connections.

options.label: C
options.text: Yes, NodeJS can be used to write general-purpose JavaScript scripts that are completely unrelated to web servers.

options.label: D
options.text: Yes, but only if the scripts use the DOM API, because NodeJS was designed as a bridge between browser JavaScript and server JavaScript.

questions.explanationMd: NodeJS is not limited to web servers. It can run ordinary JavaScript programs, command-line tools, automation scripts, and other non-web-server code.

questions.questionMd: The lecture notes describe the term **server** as overloaded. What does this mean?

options.label: A
options.text: The word "server" refers to both the DNS resolution step and the TCP handshake step that occur before any data is transferred.

options.label: B
options.text: The word "server" can refer either to the physical machine running server software or to the software program itself, depending on context.

options.label: C
options.text: The word "server" simultaneously describes the TCP protocol layer and the HTTP application layer in a network stack.

options.label: D
options.text: The word "server" is used interchangeably with "client" in modern web development because both run JavaScript code.

questions.explanationMd: An overloaded term has more than one related meaning. In web development, **server** may mean the hardware machine or the server software running on that machine.

questions.questionMd: What does calling `server.listen(3000)` do in a NodeJS HTTP server program?

options.label: A
options.text: It creates a new TCP socket on port 3000, encrypts it with TLS, and then begins forwarding HTTPS traffic to the server handler.

options.label: B
options.text: It makes the program start accepting incoming HTTP messages sent to port 3000, keeping the process running indefinitely.

options.label: C
options.text: It imports the port 3000 configuration from the operating system's network settings and applies it to the current process.

options.label: D
options.text: It sends a test HTTP request to port 3000 to verify that no other server process is already occupying that port number.

questions.explanationMd: `server.listen(3000)` tells the NodeJS server to listen for incoming requests on port 3000. The process remains active so it can continue receiving requests.

questions.questionMd: In the context of networking, what is a **socket**?

options.label: A
options.text: A numbered logical endpoint, ranging from 0 to 65535, that identifies a specific service running on a host machine.

options.label: B
options.text: A physical hardware port on a server machine used to connect network cables to the motherboard.

options.label: C
options.text: The encrypted tunnel created by HTTPS to protect data exchanged between a client browser and a remote web server.

options.label: D
options.text: One end of a communication channel through which data can be sent and received.

questions.explanationMd: A socket represents one endpoint of a network communication channel. Data can be sent and received through that endpoint.

questions.questionMd: What is **npm** primarily used for in a NodeJS development workflow?

options.label: A
options.text: It is a command-line tool that installs packages (libraries and tools) written in JavaScript and compatible with NodeJS.

options.label: B
options.text: It is a browser extension that allows developers to inspect and modify the DOM of pages served from a NodeJS backend.

options.label: C
options.text: It is a version control system integrated with NodeJS that tracks changes to JavaScript source files across a development team.

options.label: D
options.text: It is a built-in NodeJS module that provides methods for creating HTTP servers and handling incoming TCP connections.

questions.explanationMd: npm is the Node package manager. It is commonly used from the command line to install and manage JavaScript packages for NodeJS projects.

questions.questionMd: According to the lecture, what does **TCP (Transmission Control Protocol)** define?

options.label: A
options.text: The encryption standard applied to HTTPS traffic to protect data transmitted between clients and servers.

options.label: B
options.text: The structure and syntax of HTTP request and response messages exchanged between a browser and a web server.

options.label: C
options.text: The mapping between domain names and IP addresses maintained by distributed name servers across the internet.

options.label: D
options.text: The data format used for sending information over the network wire, and it can be used for HTTP, FTP, and other protocols.

questions.explanationMd: TCP is a transport-layer protocol used to send data reliably between endpoints. Application protocols such as HTTP and FTP can run over TCP.

questions.questionMd: When using the browser's `fetch()` API to send an HTTP **POST** request to `/hello`, which option correctly specifies the HTTP method?

options.label: A
options.text: `fetch('/hello', 'POST')`, passing the HTTP method as the second positional argument directly to the fetch function call.

options.label: B
options.text: `fetch('/hello', { method: 'POST' })`, passing an options object with the `method` property set to `'POST'`.

options.label: C
options.text: `fetch.post('/hello')`, which is a shorthand helper method on the fetch object specifically designed for POST requests.

options.label: D
options.text: `fetch('/hello', { type: 'POST' })`, where the `type` property in the options object overrides the default GET method.

questions.explanationMd: The `fetch()` function accepts an options object as its second argument. Setting `method: 'POST'` changes the HTTP method from the default GET to POST.

questions.questionMd: In a NodeJS HTTP request handler, what does calling `res.end()` do?

options.label: A
options.text: It writes the final message to the response body and signals to the server that the response is complete.

options.label: B
options.text: It terminates the NodeJS process and releases all bound ports back to the operating system's port pool.

options.label: C
options.text: It sets the HTTP status code of the response to 200 and automatically adds the Content-Type header to the message.

options.label: D
options.text: It closes the TCP connection and stops the server from listening for any further incoming HTTP requests on that port.

questions.explanationMd: `res.end()` finishes the HTTP response. It can send the final response data and tells NodeJS that no more response body will be written.

questions.questionMd: What is the purpose of the `require()` statement in NodeJS?

options.label: A
options.text: It loads a module into the current file, similar to `import` in Java or `include` in C++.

options.label: B
options.text: It instructs the V8 engine to pre-compile a JavaScript file into bytecode and cache it for faster future execution.

options.label: C
options.text: It sends an HTTP GET request to the npm registry to check whether a package is compatible with the current NodeJS version.

options.label: D
options.text: It declares a global variable that is shared across all JavaScript files in the same NodeJS project directory.

questions.explanationMd: `require()` is used in CommonJS-style NodeJS code to load modules, libraries, or local files into the current file.

questions.questionMd: According to the lecture, what is the default port number used for **HTTP** requests when no port is specified in a URL?

options.label: A
options.text: Port 3000, which is the standard development port used by NodeJS and ExpressJS applications running locally.

options.label: B
options.text: Port 443, which is commonly reserved for encrypted HTTPS communication between browsers and remote web servers.

options.label: C
options.text: Port 53, which is assigned to the Domain Name System service for resolving hostnames to IP addresses.

options.label: D
options.text: Port 80, which is the well-known default port for Hypertext Transfer Protocol traffic on the World Wide Web.

questions.explanationMd: The default port for ordinary HTTP traffic is port 80. HTTPS commonly uses port 443, while 3000 is often used for local development.

questions.questionMd: According to the lecture summary, after the server software receives an HTTP request, what is the correct sequence of actions it takes?

options.label: A
options.text: The server software binds to a new port, sends an HTTP GET request back to the client to confirm receipt, then closes the connection.

options.label: B
options.text: The server software parses the message, creates an HTTP response, and then the server OS sends that response to the client over TCP.

options.label: C
options.text: The server software immediately sends an empty 200 OK response and then asynchronously processes the request body in the background.

options.label: D
options.text: The server software forwards the raw TCP packet to the DNS server, which translates it and routes the reply back to the client browser.

questions.explanationMd: A typical server receives and parses an HTTP request, creates the appropriate HTTP response, and sends that response back to the client using the underlying TCP connection.

options.label: A
options.text: When a GET request is made to the path `/hello`, the server responds with the text `GET hello!`.

options.label: B
options.text: When any HTTP request arrives at the server, the response body is set to `GET hello!` regardless of the requested path.

options.label: C
options.text: When a POST request is made to the path `/hello`, the server replies with `GET hello!` to acknowledge receipt of the data.

options.label: D
options.text: When the server starts listening, it sends an HTTP GET request to the `/hello` endpoint to verify that the route is reachable.

questions.explanationMd: `app.get('/hello', ...)` registers a route handler for GET requests to `/hello`. The handler sends the response text `GET hello!`.

questions.subtopic: Raw NodeJS HTTP API vs ExpressJS
questions.questionMd: According to the lecture, why do developers prefer using **ExpressJS** over the raw NodeJS HTTP API for building servers?

options.label: A
options.text: The raw NodeJS HTTP APIs do not support JavaScript and instead require developers to write server logic in C++ directly.

options.label: B
options.text: The raw NodeJS HTTP APIs are low-level, requiring developers to manually parse requests, write responses, and handle a lot of tedious processing code.

options.label: C
options.text: The raw NodeJS HTTP APIs can only handle GET requests, so ExpressJS is required to support POST, PUT, and DELETE methods.

options.label: D
options.text: The raw NodeJS HTTP APIs are deprecated and no longer maintained, making ExpressJS the only officially supported way to build servers.

questions.explanationMd: ExpressJS provides higher-level routing and response helpers. This reduces the manual, low-level work required when using the raw NodeJS HTTP API directly.

questions.questionMd: Which command correctly executes a JavaScript file called `app.js` using NodeJS?

options.label: A
options.text: `run node --file app.js`

options.label: B
options.text: `node app.js`

options.label: C
options.text: `execute app.js --runtime node`

options.label: D
options.text: `npm start app.js`

questions.explanationMd: A JavaScript file is executed with Node.js by writing `node` followed by the filename, such as `node app.js`.

questions.questionMd: In the context of networking, what is a socket?

options.label: A
options.text: A numbered logical endpoint, ranging from 0 to 65535, that identifies a specific service running on a host machine.

options.label: B
options.text: The encrypted tunnel created by HTTPS to protect data exchanged between a client browser and a remote web server.

options.label: C
options.text: One end of a communication channel through which data can be sent and received.

options.label: D
options.text: A physical hardware port on a server machine used to connect network cables to the motherboard.

questions.explanationMd: A socket represents one endpoint of a network communication channel. It is used by software to send and receive data over a network.

questions.questionMd: What is npm primarily used for in a NodeJS development workflow?

options.label: A
options.text: It is a version control system integrated with NodeJS that tracks changes to JavaScript source files across a development team.

options.label: B
options.text: It is a command-line tool that installs packages, libraries, and tools written in JavaScript and compatible with NodeJS.

options.label: C
options.text: It is a built-in NodeJS module that provides methods for creating HTTP servers and handling incoming TCP connections.

options.label: D
options.text: It is a browser extension that allows developers to inspect and modify the DOM of pages served from a NodeJS backend.

questions.explanationMd: npm is the Node package manager. It is mainly used to install and manage JavaScript packages and development tools.

questions.questionMd: What is the V8 engine, and what role does it play in both Chrome and NodeJS?

options.label: A
options.text: It is a package manager integrated into NodeJS that downloads and manages third-party JavaScript libraries from the npm registry.

options.label: B
options.text: It is a DOM rendering engine that converts HTML and CSS into a visual pixel display inside the Chrome browser window.

options.label: C
options.text: It is the JavaScript interpreter used by both Chrome and NodeJS to parse, compile, and execute JavaScript code.

options.label: D
options.text: It is the network library embedded in Chrome that manages TCP connections and forwards HTTP messages to the operating system.

questions.explanationMd: V8 is Google's JavaScript engine. Chrome uses it to run JavaScript in the browser, and Node.js uses it to run JavaScript outside the browser.

questions.questionMd: Which curl command would you use to send an HTTP PUT request to `http://localhost:3000/hello`?

options.label: A
options.text: `curl --request PUT http://localhost:3000/hello`

options.label: B
options.text: `curl http://localhost:3000/hello --type PUT`

options.label: C
options.text: `curl --method PUT --Url http://localhost:3000/hello`

options.label: D
options.text: `curl PUT http://localhost:3000/hello`

questions.explanationMd: In curl, `--request PUT` explicitly sets the HTTP method to PUT for the specified URL.

questions.questionMd: According to the lecture, what is the recommended way to send data in a POST request rather than using query parameters in the URL?

options.label: A
options.text: Append data to the URL path as route segments instead of query parameters so Express can read them from `req.params`.

options.label: B
options.text: Send the data in the body of the HTTP request rather than appending it as query parameters to the URL.

options.label: C
options.text: Store data in the browser's local storage before making the POST request so the server can retrieve it on the next GET request.

options.label: D
options.text: Encode all data as Base64 and place it in the Authorization header so the server can decode it securely upon receipt.

questions.explanationMd: POST requests commonly send data in the request body, which avoids putting the submitted data directly in the URL query string.

questions.questionMd: The NodeJS `on()` function used on a server object is the equivalent of which browser API?

options.label: A
options.text: `document.querySelector()`, which selects DOM elements matching a given CSS selector string.

options.label: B
options.text: `setTimeout()`, which schedules a callback function to be executed after a specified delay in milliseconds.

options.label: C
options.text: `addEventListener`, which registers a callback function to handle a specific named event.

options.label: D
options.text: `fetch()`, which asynchronously sends HTTP requests from the browser to a specified URL endpoint.

questions.explanationMd: In Node.js, `.on(eventName, callback)` registers a listener for a named event, similar to `addEventListener` in browser JavaScript.

questions.questionMd: If a NodeJS server is listening on port 3000 of your local machine, which URL would you use in a browser to access it?

options.label: A
options.text: `node://localhost:3000`

options.label: C
options.text: `http://localhost:3000`

options.label: D
options.text: `http://server:3000/local`

questions.explanationMd: A local HTTP server running on port 3000 can be reached through `http://localhost:3000` in the browser.

questions.questionMd: In a basic NodeJS server, what does `http.createServer()` return?

options.label: A
options.text: An active TCP connection to the operating system that immediately begins forwarding packets to the default HTTP port 80.

options.label: B
options.text: A Promise object that resolves with the first HTTP request received after the server begins listening on the specified port.

options.label: C
options.text: An Express application instance that provides routing methods such as `app.get()` and `app.post()`.

options.label: D
options.text: A Server object that can listen for incoming HTTP requests and emit events when requests arrive.

questions.explanationMd: `http.createServer()` creates and returns a Node.js HTTP Server object. That server can then listen on a port and respond to incoming requests.

questions.questionMd: What happens when you run the `node` command in a terminal without specifying a filename?

options.label: A
options.text: It starts an interactive REPL loop where you can type and execute JavaScript expressions one at a time, similar to the Chrome console.

options.label: B
options.text: It automatically searches the current directory for a file named `index.js` and executes it as the default entry point.

options.label: C
options.text: It prints the installed NodeJS version number and a list of available built-in modules, then exits immediately.

options.label: D
options.text: It launches a local HTTP server on port 80 and waits for incoming browser connections without executing any JavaScript.

questions.explanationMd: Running `node` alone opens the Node.js REPL, an interactive prompt where JavaScript expressions can be entered and evaluated.

questions.questionMd: What is "binding" in the context of running a server process?

options.label: A
options.text: Telling the operating system which port number to associate with the server process so it can receive incoming messages.

options.label: B
options.text: Establishing a persistent TCP connection between two servers so they can exchange data without repeating the handshake.

options.label: C
options.text: Encrypting the server's IP address so that DNS queries return a hashed value instead of the actual numerical address.

options.label: D
options.text: Compiling JavaScript source code into native machine code before the NodeJS runtime begins accepting HTTP requests.

questions.explanationMd: Binding a server to a port associates that server process with the port, allowing the operating system to route incoming connections to it.

questions.questionMd: Which statement best describes server-side programming as opposed to client-side programming?

options.label: A
options.text: The code is compiled by the browser's JavaScript engine before being transmitted over TCP to the server for execution.

options.label: B
options.text: The code runs on a remote server that generates web pages and other web resources.

options.label: C
options.text: The code executes within a sandboxed environment provided by the operating system on the user's local machine.

options.label: D
options.text: The code runs inside the user's browser and is responsible for rendering HTML elements and handling DOM events directly.

questions.explanationMd: Server-side programming runs on a server and can generate pages, API responses, and other resources before sending them to clients.

questions.questionMd: According to the lecture, what does TCP (Transmission Control Protocol) define?

options.label: A
options.text: The structure and syntax of HTTP request and response messages exchanged between a browser and a web server.

options.label: B
options.text: The mapping between domain names and IP addresses maintained by distributed name servers across the internet.

options.label: C
options.text: The data format used for sending information over the network wire, and it can be used for HTTP, FTP, and other protocols.

options.label: D
options.text: The encryption standard applied to HTTPS traffic to protect data transmitted between clients and servers.

questions.explanationMd: In this lecture context, TCP is presented as the lower-level protocol used to carry data for higher-level protocols such as HTTP and FTP over the network.

questions.questionMd: How does NodeJS handle the complexity of network sockets when building a web server?

options.label: A
options.text: NodeJS delegates all socket creation to the browser's DOM API, which then forwards messages to the server program.

options.label: B
options.text: NodeJS uses the V8 engine's built-in socket library to open encrypted connections on all available network ports.

options.label: C
options.text: NodeJS requires developers to manually create and bind sockets before attaching any HTTP request listeners.

options.label: D
options.text: NodeJS abstracts socket management away so developers do not need to think about sockets directly.

questions.explanationMd: Node.js HTTP server APIs hide most low-level socket-management details, letting developers work with server and request/response abstractions instead.
